article_title: Bridging Artificial Intelligence and Power Systems Education Using a Hands-On Executable Framework
citation: Junjie Yin, Buxin She, Xinyu Feng, Fangxing (Fran) Li. (2026). Bridging Artificial Intelligence and Power Systems Education Using a Hands-On Executable Framework. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02599
title: Open executable module library of six Jupyter notebooks for AI in power systems
description: An open repository of six hands-on modules released as Jupyter notebooks that run locally or on Google Colab, spanning three tiers: DNN templates for function approximation and load-curve fitting, a CNN power-flow surrogate for the PJM 5-bus system, and frontier modules on DNN-assisted optimization, DRL battery storage control, and PINNs for the swing equation. "Every module follows the same notebook skeleton: aSettingsblock (Section 0), data generation, model construction, training, evaluation, and visualization." Modules ship with small defaults, pinned environments, and one-click Colab execution, and are delivered through an IEEE online course and IEEE PES webinars.
requirements: A pinned environment specification and one-click Colab execution for exact reproducibility
constraints: The present modules are intentionally lightweight, with small demonstration settings chosen for speed rather than realism
target_learners: beginners, students, engineers, and interdisciplinary learners in power and energy systems
target_learning_goals: supervised-learning workflow, surrogate modeling, learned-constraint optimization, deep reinforcement learning control, and physics-informed learning
examples: Early deployment drew more than 590 live webinar attendees in Part I, among the ten most-attended IEEE PES webinars, and over 344 repository visits within two weeks.
key_sources: Junjie Yin, Buxin She, Xinyu Feng, Fangxing (Fran) Li. (2026). Bridging Artificial Intelligence and Power Systems Education Using a Hands-On Executable Framework. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02599

article_title: Walking the number line: towards an enactive understanding of integer arithmetic
citation: Jacqueline Anton, Dor Abrahamson. (2025). Walking the number line: towards an enactive understanding of integer arithmetic. Instructional Science. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11251-025-09707-w
title: Perspectival coordination framework: egocentric-to-allocentric coordination as the cognitive process of symbol grounding in embodied mathematics designs
description: The article proposes that embodied designs stage a coordination between an egocentric perspective, in which actions are experienced with respect to one's own body, and an allocentric perspective, in which objects are experienced with respect to other objects. Following Benally et al., it distinguishes "in perspectival substitution, one perspective replaces the other; in perspectival mutuality, individuals use an alternative perspective to validate their own; in perspectival synergy, a combination of two perspectives results in one that is greater than each perspective alone." The design operationalizes this as walking a body-scale number line (egocentric) then puppeteering a figurine on a desk-scale line (allocentric).
requirements: Students must experience the egocentric enaction first and then be guided to coordinate it with the allocentric normative display
constraints: Merely shifting unidirectionally from the BNL to a figurine on the SNL was often not enough, per the article's implications
target_learning_goals: understanding addition and subtraction with positive and negative integers
examples: Students walked the body-scale number line, then moved a puppy figurine on a desk-scale number line to mimic their movements
key_sources: Jacqueline Anton, Dor Abrahamson. (2025). Walking the number line: towards an enactive understanding of integer arithmetic. Instructional Science. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11251-025-09707-w

article_title: Learning potential in youth's online networks: A multilevel approach
citation: Ünlüsoy, A., de Haan, M.J., Leander, K., & Völker, B. (2013). Learning potential in youth's online networks: A multilevel approach. Computers & Education, 69, 522-533. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compedu.2013.06.007
title: Ego-network approach for mapping youth online networks.
description: The study applied an ego-network approach to map the online personal networks of youth from various ethnic backgrounds and education levels living in the Netherlands, collecting information on network contacts and their interactions.
requirements: collection of information on network contacts including age, gender, location and interactions
target_learning_goals: informal learning through online personal networks

article_title: Effects of Geographic Information System on the Learning of Environmental Education Concepts in Basic Computer-Mediated Classrooms in Nigeria
citation: Adeleke, A. G. (2017). Effects of Geographic Information System on the Learning of Environmental Education Concepts in Basic Computer-Mediated Classrooms in Nigeria. IAFOR Journal of Education, 5(3), 125-136. https://iafor.org/archives/2017/ijedu/volume-5-issue-3/
title: Envi-Geo Info System (EGIS) package: a self-developed computer-mediated instructional package integrating environmental education concepts into social studies
description: The Envi-Geo Info System (EGIS) package is a self-developed computer-mediated instructional package containing "environmental education induced concepts in social studies subject". It was built using a taxonomy based on Bloom's principles as revised by Anderson and Krathwohl (2001) in Wilson (2013), and its source code is provided in the article's appendix, written in C-Sharp. The package served as the primary treatment instrument, delivered within computer-mediated classrooms to integrate GIS-based environmental education into basic social studies teaching.
requirements: Computer-mediated classrooms with the necessary hardware and software to run the EGIS package
constraints: The study concluded that "while EGIS seems not feasible for adoption into teaching -learning process in Nigeria momentarily"
target_learners: Junior secondary school pupils in Nigeria
target_learning_goals: Environmental education concepts within basic social studies
examples: Used as the treatment instrument across four intact computer-mediated classrooms in south-west Nigeria
key_sources: Adeleke, A. G. (2017). Effects of Geographic Information System on the Learning of Environmental Education Concepts in Basic Computer-Mediated Classrooms in Nigeria. IAFOR Journal of Education, 5(3), 125-136. https://iafor.org/archives/2017/ijedu/volume-5-issue-3/

article_title: European training requirements in geriatric medicine 2025: driving competency-based education and harmonisation across Europe.
citation: Romero Ortuño R, van Iersel M, Nuotio MS, Kolk H, Topinková E, Schoevaerdts D, Farré Mercadé MV, Graf C, Cotobal Rodeles S, Vassallo MA, Vassallo M, Lütje D, Macijauskienė J, on behalf of the UEMS Geriatric Medicine Section (UEMS-GMS). (2026). European training requirements in geriatric medicine 2025: driving competency-based education and harmonisation across Europe. European Geriatric Medicine 17(2):417–428. https://doi.org/10.1007/s41999-025-01393-8
title: European Geriatric Medicine Specialty Exam (EGeMSE) as a pan-European knowledge benchmark
description: The EGeMSE is a knowledge-based online examination organised by the UEMS-GMS in cooperation with the British Geriatrics Society and the Federation of Royal Colleges of Physicians of the UK. It "consists of two three-hour online papers in English, each comprising 100 best-of-five multiple-choice questions", and successful candidates receive the post-nominal title ESE (Geriatric Medicine). The 2025 ETR formally endorses it as a pan-European benchmark of theoretical knowledge supporting harmonised certification. The inaugural exam took place on April 23, 2025.
requirements: Organisational cooperation between UEMS-GMS, BGS and the UK Royal Colleges
constraints: It is designed to complement rather than replace existing national knowledge-based assessments
it represents a standard of knowledge rather than of skills or competencies
target_learners: EU and non-EU doctors in training or qualified specialists in geriatric medicine
target_learning_goals: demonstration of theoretical knowledge in geriatric medicine at a European standard
examples: In some countries (e.g. Switzerland and Ireland at the time of writing) the EGeMSE has already been recognised by national competent authorities as a valid alternative or supplement to domestic examinations
key_sources: Romero Ortuño R, van Iersel M, Nuotio MS, Kolk H, Topinková E, Schoevaerdts D, Farré Mercadé MV, Graf C, Cotobal Rodeles S, Vassallo MA, Vassallo M, Lütje D, Macijauskienė J, on behalf of the UEMS Geriatric Medicine Section (UEMS-GMS). (2026). European training requirements in geriatric medicine 2025: driving competency-based education and harmonisation across Europe. European Geriatric Medicine 17(2):417–428. https://doi.org/10.1007/s41999-025-01393-8

article_title: Multi-Layer Perception model with Elastic Grey Wolf Optimization to predict student achievement.
citation: Song Yinqiu, Meng Xianqiu, Jiang Jianhua. (2022). Multi-Layer Perception model with Elastic Grey Wolf Optimization to predict student achievement. PLoS One. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0276943
title: EGWO-MLP student achievement prediction model
description: The EGWO-MLP model is a Multi-Layer Perceptron whose weights and biases are optimized by the EGWO algorithm to predict student achievement. It contains "an input layer, two hidden layers, and an output layer", with 30 UCI Student Performance attributes as input nodes and student grades as output. The article states the model "can predict and warn students, which is conducive to assisting teachers in managing and helping students" and that it is feasible for predicting student achievement.
requirements: Training and verification based on the thirty attributes from the UCI Machine Learning Repository student performance dataset, with 80% training data and 20% testing data
constraints: Evaluated in MATLAB R2015b with population 10 and max iteration 300, twenty runs per setting; prediction relies on structured data
target_learners: secondary school students in two Portuguese schools
target_learning_goals: predicting final subject achievement (Mathematics and Portuguese)
examples: Twenty runs for each working setting; compared against AGWO-MLP, PSO-MLP, GA-MLP, BA-MLP, DE-MLP, SCA-MLP, and basic GWO-MLP
key_sources: Song Yinqiu, Meng Xianqiu, Jiang Jianhua. (2022). Multi-Layer Perception model with Elastic Grey Wolf Optimization to predict student achievement. PLoS One. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0276943
